  MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing
  Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  July 14, 2026
  A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
  Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Bucknum at
  5:00 p.m., on July 14, 2026, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

  A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00
  p.m. on July 9, 2026, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at the Montanoso
  Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray Community and Senior
  Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

  *All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

  Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Ruesch
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell
  Mayor Bucknum

  Absent:  None

  Staff Present:  Elaine Lister, City Manager
  Jerry Hill, Assistant City Manager
  Tarquin Preziosi, City Attorney
  Ellis Chang, Director of Administrative Services
  Alison Walker, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

  CS1.  Conference with Real Property Negotiators: Government Code Section 54956.8.
  Property: Los Osos, 25282 Marguerite Parkway, APN 782-011-95. Agency Negotiators:
  Elaine Lister, City Manager, Jerry Hill, Assistant City Manager, and Tarquin Preziosi,
  City Attorney. Negotiating Parties: Regency Centers and Paragon Commercial Group
  LLC. Under Negotiation: Price and Terms

  CS2.  Annual Public Employee Performance Evaluations. Government Code § 54957(b)(1):
  Titles - City Manager and Assistant City Manager

  City Council Minutes  1  July 14, 2026
 Docusign Envelope ID: A9210BFC-812B-8900-8255-AEEBA2F8D4BF

  CS3.  Conference with Legal Counsel - Pending Litigation.  Government Code §
  54956.9(d)(1): Southern California Edison Co. v. City of Mission Viejo, OCSC Case No.
  30-2026-01573209-CU-NP-WJC

  RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

  At the hour of 5:01 p.m. Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting. At the hour of 6:08 p.m. Mayor
  Bucknum reconvened the meeting with all five Council Members present.

  REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

  City Attorney Preziosi announced that there were three properly agendized items with no reportable
  action.

  INVOCATION: Mayor Bucknum

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

  PRESENTATIONS

  P1.  Recognize Mission Viejo Little Leagues

  Mayor Bucknum presented proclamations to the Mission Viejo Little Leagues.

  P2.  Business Spotlight - A-Z Tech Automotive

  Mayor Bucknum presented proclamation to A-Z Tech Automotive.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Bryan Zahn. M.V.: Commended the City Council, Nieves Landscape, and Public Services for
  maintaining local Little League facilities, and recognized District Administrator Ezio Petrella for his
  long-standing service.

  Zoey Ammerman: Introduced "fairness" as the month's character topic, speaking on the importance of
  gender and racial equity in the community.

  Tom Moore, M.V.: Commented on the Planning and Transportation Commission's recent housing
  element discussions, urging the Council to take a new approach.

  Faith Fersten, M.V.: Raised ongoing safety and fire hazard concerns regarding a neighboring property
  on Via Santa Maria and inquired about upcoming hearing notifications.

  Andy Steen: Announced that the Mission Viejo High School Marching Band and Color Guard will host
  a Western Band Association competition on October 17, 2026, and called for community volunteers.

  City Council Minutes  2  July 14, 2026
 Docusign Envelope ID: A9210BFC-812B-8900-8255-AEEBA2F8D4BF

  Michael Rotcher, M.V.: Discussed a petition regarding an "Our Declaration of Interdependence"
  presentation submitted to federal representatives and shared commentary on local free speech
  provisions.

  Carolyn Gatto, M.V.: Spoke on themes related to the "Declaration of Interdependence" petition, offering
  remarks on the current presidential administration.

  Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Requested that Planning and Transportation Commission meetings be
  livestreamed, the live police blotter be reinstated on the city website, and a citizen oversight committee
  be formed for Flock safety cameras.

  Laura Lacko, M.V.: Addressed a false rumor regarding a library disturbance, questioned the net revenue
  generated to offset the over $22,000 city expenditure on triathlon security, and raised data privacy
  concerns regarding Flock safety cameras, citing the LAPD's discontinuation of their contract.

  City Attorney Preziosi provided an update on the hoarding property on Via Santa Maria, and stated that
  the hearing would take place in the next 15-20 days and information will be provided on the City’s
  website.

  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Item 12 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ruesch to approve the Consent
  Calendar outlined below.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the Regular City Council Meeting of June 23, 2026, as presented.

  2.  General Check Register Dated June 12, June 19, & June 26, 2026

  Ratified the accompanying check registers.

  3.  Golf Check Register June 12, June 19, & June 26, 2026

  Ratified the accompanying check registers.

  City Council Minutes  3  July 14, 2026
 Docusign Envelope ID: A9210BFC-812B-8900-8255-AEEBA2F8D4BF

  4.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for May 2026

  Received and filed.

  5.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for May 2026

  Received and filed.

  6.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for May 2026

  Received and filed.

  7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for May 2026

  Received and filed.

  8.  Installation of (3) Shade Structures for the Animal Services Department

  Approved Resolution 26-37 Amending the Fiscal Year 2025/26 Budget for the installation
  of three (3) shade structures for the Animal Services Center.

  9.  2026 Residential Resurfacing—Asphalt Repairs and Asphalt Overlays (CIP 27838)—
  Award of Contract

  Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to R.J. Noble Company (A26-25)
  in the amount of $1,293,400.00.

  10.  Renewed Measure M Public Works Seven-Year Capital Improvement Program

  Adopted Resolution 26-38 adopting a Renewed Measure M (M2) Seven-Year Capital
  Improvement Program (CIP), beginning with the 2026/2027 fiscal year, to satisfy the City’s
  eligibility requirements of the Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) M2
  Program.

  11.  Marguerite Parkway/La Sierra Drive Acceleration Lane Project (CIP 26270)-Award of
  Contract

  Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to Van Engineering, Inc. (A26-20)
  in the amount of $228,720.

  13.  Annual Routine Monthly Landscape Maintenance - Contract Area 8 – Oso Creek Golf
  Course

  City Council Minutes  4  July 14, 2026
 Docusign Envelope ID: A9210BFC-812B-8900-8255-AEEBA2F8D4BF

  (1) Approved Third Amendment to the existing maintenance contract with Nieves Landscape,
  LLC.; and (2) authorized the issuance of a change order to the existing Purchase Order for
  Landscape Contract Area 8 to Nieves Landscape, LLC. in an amount not to exceed
  $285,000.00.

  14.  Technical Services Outsourcing Renewal for Mission Viejo Library02.

  (1) Approved first amendment to existing agreement with Ingram Library Services, LLC
  (A25-34C) for customized library services including cataloging and processing of library
  materials for the period of July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2028 (years 3 and 4), adding an amount
  not to exceed $300,000 to the original contract; and (2) authorized issuance of purchase orders
  to Ingram Library Services, LLC for an amount not to exceed $300,000.

  ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

  12.  Oso Creek Golf Course – Purchase of Replacement Electric Greens Triplex Mower

  Assistant City Manager Jerry Hill presented the staff report.

  Mayor Bucknum asked for any council questions.
  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell wanted to highlight this item for the community. Council Member
  Ruesch spoke about the benefits this mower will provide.

  The following spoke on this item:

  Peter Molinari, M.V.: Spoke regarding his support of this item to benefit Oso Creek but also
  residents in the surrounding neighborhoods as electric mowers are much quieter to operate.

  Motion made by Council Member Ruesch, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, to (1)
  approve purchase for the replacement of the Oso Creek Golf Course Greens Mower to Stotz
  Equipment in an amount not to exceed $93,936.05; and (2) authorize staff to issue a purchase
  order to Stotz Equipment for a not to exceed amount of $93,936.05.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  PUBLIC HEARING

  15.  Approval of Resolution for Property Tax Correction Between City of Mission Viejo
  and Laguna Niguel

  City Council Minutes  5  July 14, 2026
 Docusign Envelope ID: A9210BFC-812B-8900-8255-AEEBA2F8D4BF

  Director of Administrative Services Ellis Chang presented the staff report.

  Mayor Bucknum opened the Public Hearing at 7:13 p.m. There being no requests to speak
  on this item Mayor Bucknum closed the Public Hearing at 7:16 p.m.

  City Attorney Preziosi presented supplemental information to the staff report.

  Mayor Bucknum asked for any council questions.

  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell inquired about the annual amount.

  Mayor Bucknum closed the public hearing.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ruesch to adopt
  Resolution 26-39 approving the Ad Valorem Property Tax Revenue Allocation Agreement
  and Release to prospectively correct property tax allocation pursuant to Revenue and
  Taxation Code sections 99(b)(6) and 99.02.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

  NEW BUSINESS

  16.  Request of Four Homeowners Association Board of Directors to Manage Pest Control
  by All Authorized Means, Including Firearms

  Emergency Operations Manager Paul Catsimanes presented the staff report.

  June Anderson: Member of Casa Del Sol Homeowners Association, spoke regarding her
  support of this item and emphasized the destruction that these wildlife pests can cause.

  Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Spoke regarding her support of this item and agreed it is the most
  humane way to handle these pests.

  Motion made by Mayor Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1) approve the
  request of Casta Del Sol Homeowners Association for a variance that will allow the
  association to manage on-site nuisance wildlife by the most humane means possible for the
  health, safety and welfare of the community; (2) approve the request of Mission Viejo
  Environmental Association for a variance that will allow the association to manage on-site
  nuisance wildlife by the most humane means possible for the health, safety and welfare of the
  community; (3) approve the request of Palmia Masters Association for a variance that will
  allow the association to manage on-site nuisance wildlife by the most humane means possible
  for the health, safety and welfare of the community; and (4) approve the request of Tres Vistas

  by the most humane means possible for the health, safety and welfare of the community.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

  MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

  17.  Transportation Corridor Agencies (TCA) Report

  Council Member Kelley provided the report and announced that TCA recently received top
  honors at the ACC-OC Leadership Summit and Golden Hub of Innovation Awards. The 24191
  express connector project partnership was recognized in the transportation, innovation, and
  mobility solutions category, highlighting the collaboration, perseverance, and being a good
  example of regional partnership that has helped to advance this long-envisioned project which
  will be so beneficial to regional mobility.

  CITY MANAGER REPORTS

  City Manager Lister gave an update on Wholesome Choice and stated they are hoping to have a grand
  opening on Labor Day. She also stated that there is a golf simulator that is currently going through plan
  check.

  CITY ATTORNEY REPORTS

  City Attorney Preziosi shared that a private disability rights group has filed a new state court lawsuit
  against the City of Costa Mesa challenging its sober living home ordinance, despite the city's previous
  successes defending the ordinance in federal court. If successful, the lawsuit seeks to declare the
  ordinance in violation of state and federal fair housing laws, which would set it aside and repeal
  enforcement - potentially impacting similar ordinances in other cities like Mission Viejo. This update
  was presented to the City Council for informational purposes only, requiring no action at this time.

  COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

  18.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended - AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

  City Council Minutes  7  July 14, 2026
 Docusign Envelope ID: A9210BFC-812B-8900-8255-AEEBA2F8D4BF

  Council Member Kelley

  Council Member Kelley reported on several positive recent community events, including the grand
  opening of the nation's first standalone Costco gas station and a new upscale appliance store. Key
  highlights included attending the Golden Hub Awards, celebrating the Fourth of July with a successful
  street fair, parade, and the unveiling of the America 250 Obelisk, and honoring senior volunteers at the
  SCOR awards luncheon. Additionally, Council Member Kelley noted the strong turnout for the three-
  day barbecue music fest at Oso Viejo Park and reminded residents to look out for upcoming summer
  concerts in July.

  Council Member Ruesch

  Council Member Ruesch thanked staff, committees, and participants for making the recent parade a
  resounding success with great community feedback. He also shared that discussions with Costco
  principals during the new gas station opening hinted at a potential future car wash addition on the site.
  Finally, he noted that traffic around the new center has been smooth and negligible, encouraging
  residents to support the local businesses and fill up there.

  Council Member Vasquez

  Council Member Vasquez shared that she visited the new Costco gas station prior to its grand opening
  and encouraged her family to shop locally to keep tax dollars in Mission Viejo. She also highlighted the
  tremendous success of Mission Viejo Pride event, which drew about 2,000 attendees with over 80 booths,
  great family programming, and line and salsa dancing. Additionally, she enjoyed the Fourth of July street
  fair and parade, served as a judge for the professional pitmasters at the barbecue festival, and recounted
  a wonderful two-week belated 20th anniversary trip to Bali.

  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell announced that the Sports and Economic Tourism Committee is meeting to
  discuss updates, including Slovakia's strong interest in using Mission Viejo as a training base for the 2028
  Olympics. He also shared highlights from the Fourth of July celebrations, including riding in a '57 Chevy
  convertible with his wife in the parade and judging the professional chef rib competition at the successful
  festival. Finally, he commended the city staff, Mr. Nix, Assistance City Manager Jerry Hill, and their
  teams for the meticulous planning and execution of the events.

  Mayor Bucknum

  Mayor Bucknum endorsed the new Costco fuel station as a convenient stop for locals and visitors alike,
  and noted the city's nomination at the Leadership Summit's Golden Hub of Innovation Awards. She also
  highlighted recent community events, including the '90s Night at Oso Creek Golf Course, the Lei'd Back
  Luau at Montanoso, and the Fourth of July celebrations, where she rode in a classic Lincoln Continental
  and praised the seamless organization of the parade and barbecue music fest. Additionally, she requested
  an update from the Orange County Sheriff's Department regarding flock cameras and the police blotter.
  She promoted the upcoming Chamber business expo and Tijuana Dogs concert.

  City Council Minutes  8  July 14, 2026
 Docusign Envelope ID: A9210BFC-812B-8900-8255-AEEBA2F8D4BF

  ADJOURNMENT

  At the hour of 7:47 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor
  Bucknum adjourned the meeting in memory of Joie Gendron, to Tuesday, August 25, 2026, at 5:00 p.m.
